verdict.rationale: CodeRabbit keeps its automation and review behavior as config-as-code. Settings live in a `.coderabbit.yaml` file, which can sit in a dedicated org-wide `coderabbit` repository, and the product can print the resolved configuration as YAML on any PR. That makes the automation definitions versionable and reviewable through the repository, but versioning and rollback come from git rather than from documented CodeRabbit features. Missing for 10: first-party version history for automations/recipes, an explicit review or approval flow for config changes, documented rollback, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: Maintain CodeRabbit configuration for your entire organization in one dedicated repository. Create a `coderabbit` repository in your organization and add your `.coderabbit.yaml` file
Use the `@coderabbitai configuration` command on any PR to get the resolved configuration in YAML format.
Configure when and how CodeRabbit automatically reviews pull requests using the `reviews.auto_review` settings.
